baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.summary: A flightless diving bird. Breeding on sea ice and cooperative huddling help it persist in a cold environment.

anatomy.name: Flippers
anatomy.description: Source feathered flippers have smoothly bound shoulders. Left and right flippers stroke together dorsoventrally underwater; the outer blades stay stiff. Angle and amplitude are authored.

anatomy.name: Adult plumage
anatomy.description: The selected artist feather images are retained. Shorter bill and flipper proportions, paler yellow vertex-color adjustments and a pink lower-bill panel adapt its king-like traits toward an emperor exterior. This is an artist interpretation, not a measured live-animal morphometric fit.

anatomy.name: Feet and support
anatomy.description: The selected source retains two webbed feet, claws and short visible tarsi. Feet alternate support on land and trail while swimming; they are not the main propulsors. No display ground is included.

behaviors.label: Walk
behaviors.description: Four short alternating steps with the stance foot held in world space and a modest side-to-side shift. Both feet remain attached beneath the plumage and end supported. Step size, roll and timing are authored; no measured contact forces or gait speed is implied. Playback now stops at eight seconds; phase buttons, pause, reverse seeking and replay expose the existing authored sequence. Display time is not an observed bout duration.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated illustrative display seconds; no biological clock

rendering.reason: Research-informed external articulation; not full physiology, fluid dynamics or independently validated kinematics.

behaviors.label: Swim
behaviors.description: Paired shoulder-driven flipper strokes on a streamlined belly-down exterior, both feet trailing. Active cycles use 1.47 Hz, the mean dominant cycle frequency from nine free-ranging emperor penguins in Sato et al. 2010. The authored eight-second demonstration settles into a glide; angles, amplitude and translational speed are not fitted to tracked animals. Playback now stops at eight seconds; phase buttons, pause, reverse seeking and replay expose the existing authored sequence. Display time is not an observed bout duration. Visual review still shows an unnatural shoulder contour in the swimming morph; that surface requires a separate rig/morph correction.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated sequence timing; active cycle 1.47 Hz referenced to one emperor field dataset

rendering.reason: Research-informed external articulation; not full physiology, fluid dynamics or independently validated kinematics. Visual review still shows an unnatural shoulder contour in the swimming morph; that surface requires a separate rig/morph correction.

behaviors.label: Rest posture
behaviors.description: Quiet upright posture with flippers close to the flanks and a small authored head inclination; no egg, chick or brood-patch physiology is simulated.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated illustrative display seconds; no biological clock

behaviors.label: Underwater glide
behaviors.description: Held streamlined underwater posture, bill directed forward, paired flippers extended and both feet trailing. No continuous stroking or foot-paddling propulsion; water forces and buoyancy are not calculated. Visual review still shows an unnatural shoulder contour in the swimming morph; that surface requires a separate rig/morph correction.

sources.title: University of Michigan · Animal Diversity Web
sources.scope: Species account: written natural history and biological processes. It does not validate the 3D model.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons photographic reference
sources.scope: Photograph or micrograph, specimen caption and asset attribution; not a validation of the 3D model

sources.title: Griffin & Kram (2000) · Penguin waddling is not wasteful
sources.scope: Author-hosted full paper: five walking emperor penguins on a force platform; lateral motion and energy exchange. Our in-place foot proxy targets/sway do not reproduce those measured force, center-of-mass, energy or timing data.

sources.title: New Zealand Birds Online · Emperor penguin identification
sources.scope: Adult external appearance and qualitative natural-history context; no model certification or metric fit.

sources.title: Williams et al. (2012) · Emperor penguin muscle energy stores and stroke rates
sources.scope: Measured emperor-penguin stroke variation and stroke/glide context. Model does not calculate muscle oxygen, metabolites or dive limits.

sources.title: Australian Antarctic Program · Emperor penguin
sources.scope: Morphology, cold adaptation and huddling context. Heat exchange and social behavior are not simulated.

sources.title: Sato et al. (2007) · Stroke frequency, but not swimming speed, is related to body size in free-ranging seabirds, pinnipeds and cetaceans
sources.scope: Includes emperor penguin stroke-frequency data and broader penguin upstroke/downstroke propulsion context. Model angles, duration, force, speed and buoyancy are not fitted to these measurements.

sources.title: Australian Antarctic Program · Emperor penguin and penguin adaptations
sources.scope: Adult exterior and posture reference. Authored geometry and display timing are not measured biological validation.

sources.title: Marcel Porsiel · emperor penguin artist model
sources.scope: Artist morphology and feather images, adapted for emperor traits; not a measured specimen or proof of species identity.

sources.title: Sato et al. 2010 · Scaling of swim speed and stroke frequency
sources.scope: Table 2: mean dominant stroke cycle frequency 1.47 Hz in nine free-ranging emperors; 1.35 Hz in a separate seven-bird Penguin Ranch dataset. Only the active cycle frequency is borrowed; no universal frequency, joint angles or swimming speed is claimed.

sources.title: van Dam et al. 2002 · Stroke frequencies of emperor penguins diving under sea ice
sources.scope: Intermittent stroking and prolonged gliding. The displayed eight-second sequence is authored and is not a complete dive.

sources.title: New Zealand Birds Online · Emperor penguin identification
sources.scope: Broader paler neck patch and shorter bill distinguish emperor from king; pink lower-bill panel and adult exterior reference.

visual.fidelity: Uses the user-selected Marcel Porsiel exterior and its original feather images and UVs. Adds a bound seven-joint skeleton, continuous streamlined water posture, shorter bill and flippers, pink lower-bill and paler yellow vertex-color corrections. Two webbed feet remain visible. Walking uses alternating planted support; swimming uses paired stiff-flipper strokes followed by a glide. No display ground.
visual.scale: normalized display size; not a measurement

viewerRig.type: Seven-joint bound skeleton and continuous swimming-posture morph
viewerRig.scope: Qualitative locomotion; 1.47 Hz active cycle referenced to Sato et al. 2010 table 2. No calibrated speed, thrust, energetics, thermoregulation or complete physiology.
viewerRig.description: Selected Marcel Porsiel feathered exterior with a new bound rig. Choose Walk or Swim to play the movement study. Swimming straightens the body and neck, keeps the belly down and trails both feet; paired flippers settle into a glide. Active stroke cycle: 1.47 Hz from an emperor field study; joint angles and step timing are authored.

review.status: Selected artist exterior adapted and articulated; all-side pose inspection; independent scientific validation pending

visualAudit.scope: Individual texture/anatomical-view/posture inspection and qualitative support/flight review; expert validation pending.

remaining: Artist exterior anatomy and joint angles remain unmeasured.

No aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, metabolic, oxygen, thermal or ground-force simulation.

review.movementStudyScope: Finite playback and phase controls for existing bird articulation. Source surfaces, textures and trajectories retained; no new physiological validation.
